extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent examiners, IP practitioners, policymakers, and stakeholders concerned with U.S. patent subject matter eligibility
extracted.subtask_description: Determining whether a claimed invention is eligible subject matter under U.S. law (35 U.S.C. 101) by reference to statutory categories and judicially-created exceptions, and applying USPTO guidance and Court jurisprudence (including the Mayo/Alice two-step framework).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory basis: 35 U.S.C. 101
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent eligibility in the United States is statutorily defined by 35 U.S.C. 101; this section of the law outlines the basic criteria for patentable subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 35 U.S.C. 101 as the foundational statute when assessing whether claimed subject matter falls within the scope of patent-eligible inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory categories of patentable subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress deemed four categories of invention to be the appropriate subject matter of a patent—process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should be analyzed to determine whether they fall within one of these four statutory categories (process, machine, manufacture, composition of matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicially-created exceptions to eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Supreme Court carved out certain exceptions to patent eligibility for abstract ideas, laws of nature, and natural phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating claims, identify whether the claimed subject matter falls within one of these judicial exceptions; such exceptions are excluded from patentable subject matter even if they otherwise fall within a statutory category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step test (Mayo/Alice framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recent Court decisions have interpreted the provisions of 35 U.S.C. 101 by articulating a two-step test to distinguish eligible subject matter from subject matter that falls within one of the exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the two-step Mayo/Alice framework as articulated in Supreme Court and subsequent Federal Circuit decisions when determining eligibility; this framework is central to current jurisprudence and USPTO practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO subject matter eligibility guidance for examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO’s subject matter eligibility guidance explains how USPTO personnel, including patent examiners, should evaluate claims for patent subject matter eligibility under 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the USPTO’s internal guidance documents and any revised guidance (e.g., the 2019 Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance) for claim examination practice; the USPTO updates and clarifies examiner procedures in light of evolving case law and stakeholder input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of evolving jurisprudence and stakeholder input
rubrics_metrics.description: In the face of emerging technologies and as legal standards continue to evolve, the USPTO engages with stakeholders, Congress, and the public regarding policy aspects of patent subject matter eligibility (including reports, Federal Register notices, public comments, and roundtables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and examination practices may reflect input from reports to Congress, public comments to Federal Register notices, empirical analyses (e.g., 'Adjusting to Alice'), and public roundtables; practitioners should be aware that guidance and interpretations can change based on such processes.
